items.name: primary-button
items.title: Primary Button
items.description: The default call-to-action button, solid fill with a hover and focus state.

items.name: ghost-button
items.title: Ghost Button
items.description: A lower-emphasis outline button for secondary actions.

items.name: toggle-switch
items.title: Toggle Switch
items.description: An accessible on/off switch built on a native button with role="switch".

items.name: text-field
items.title: Text Field
items.description: A labeled text input with clear focus and placeholder states.

items.name: icon-button
items.title: Icon Button
items.description: A square icon-only button with a spring-in tooltip and a tap wiggle.

items.name: select
items.title: Select
items.description: A custom listbox with a sliding highlight and staggered option entrance, built on real ARIA combobox semantics.

items.name: checkbox
items.title: Checkbox
items.description: An accessible checkbox with a spring-drawn checkmark and a small tick-particle burst on check.

items.name: slider
items.title: Slider
items.description: A range input with a value-reactive gradient fill, a color-matched thumb glow, and a tooltip that appears while dragging.

items.name: otp-input
items.title: OTP Input
items.description: A one-time-code field as a real controlled input: type and it auto advances, Backspace steps back and clears, arrow keys plus Home and End move between boxes, and a full code pasted into any box gets split across the row with a left-to-right stagger (it tells a multi-character jump, real paste or SMS autofill, apart from ordinary typing). Each digit springs in, the active empty box carries its own blinking caret, and a completed code runs a wave down the row before resolving to a green ripple on success or a shake on a wrong code. Masked mode, `autoComplete="one-time-code"` on the first box, per-box `aria-label`s, and a reduced-motion path that drops the wave and shake for a color change.

items.name: combobox
items.title: Combobox
items.description: A multi-select typeahead with the matching logic on show, not hidden: a subsequence scorer with contiguity, word-start and short-target bonuses ranks and reorders the list as you type ("nxt" finds Next.js, "clkh" finds ClickHouse), bolds the matched letters in place, and prints a three-bar strength meter per row. Results stay grouped with sticky headers, arrow keys drive a spring-slid highlight (shared `layoutId`), Enter toggles, and Backspace on an empty field pops the last chip. Selected values are chips that spring in and out and reflow the field; a `loading` prop shows a shimmer list, no exact match offers an inline Create row (`onCreate`), and `multiple={false}` turns it into a single-select that closes on pick. Real `role="combobox"` / `listbox` / `option` wiring with `aria-activedescendant`, and a reduced-motion path that drops the slide and chip springs.

items.name: radio-group
items.title: Radio Group
items.description: The single-choice-from-a-few control the library was missing (Pill Tabs covers the segmented case). Card-style options with a label, description, right-aligned hint, and an optional badge. Proper `role="radiogroup"` with roving tabindex: one Tab stop, then arrow keys in any direction plus Home and End move the selection and wrap, skipping disabled options. The selected card lifts, its dot springs in, a check fades in, and an emerald ring slides between cards on a shared `layoutId`; reduced motion keeps the ring and drops the slide.

items.name: search-input
items.title: Search Input
items.description: A search field with the parts people always end up hand-rolling: the leading magnifier crossfades to a spinner while a debounced `onSearch` is in flight (configurable `debounceMs`), a clear button springs in once there is text and Escape clears, an optional `resultCount` renders a live pill, and a `shortcut` key (like the slash key) focuses the field from anywhere on the page with a `kbd` hint that hides once focused. Custom focus ring with the browser outline suppressed, and a reduced-motion path.

items.name: copy-button
items.title: Copy Button
items.description: Copy to clipboard as its own component instead of a snippet buried in a code block. Real `navigator.clipboard.writeText` with a hidden-textarea `execCommand` fallback; on success the icon spring-morphs from copy to check, a ring pulses out with a four-dot particle burst, an `aria-live` region announces it, and the state resets after `timeout`. Icon-only or labelled through the `variant` prop, and a reduced-motion path that keeps the icon swap and drops the burst.

items.name: color-picker
items.title: Color Picker
items.description: A self-contained HSV colour picker in a popover, with no native colour input and no OS dialog: a saturation and brightness field, a hue rail, a hex field that accepts partial typing, and a preset row. The field and rail are real ARIA sliders with pointer capture and arrow-key control (Shift for coarser steps); the popover closes on Escape or an outside click. Controlled by a hex string via `value` and `onChange`. Inline hex and HSV maths, no colour library. Used by Gradient Canvas.

items.name: intent-aware-button
items.title: Intent-Aware Button
items.description: A delete button that reads hesitation instead of just clicks: genuinely tracked cursor proximity, not a mock. Pause over it and a warning line expands in; drift toward it and back twice and it escalates to 'Are you sure?'; only a real press-and-hold, with an animated fill, commits the destructive action.

items.name: document-upload
items.title: Document Upload
items.description: A drag-and-drop dropzone backed by a real native file input, in single- or multiple-file mode via the `multiple` prop; a genuine sonar-pulse checkmark confirms every add, files get a type-aware icon (the same emerald/amber split Attachments uses), and each one lists with a delete button to remove it before it's used.

items.name: share-card
items.title: Share Card
items.description: The unfurled preview card a recipient sees when a shared Claude or ChatGPT conversation link lands somewhere else: a platform badge, title, fade-clamped snippet, and message count, with a spring pop-in and lift on hover.

items.name: share-sheet
items.title: Share Sheet
items.description: The dialog that produces that card: a sliding Only you / Anyone with the link toggle reveals a real clipboard-copy link row (the button icon morphs link-to-check) and a live preview of the resulting share card, so the two pieces are shown as one flow.

items.name: hover-border-gradient
items.title: Hover Border Gradient
items.description: A button ringed by a rotating conic-gradient comet that speeds up on hover or focus.

items.name: notification-button
items.title: Notification Button
items.description: An icon button ringed by the hover-gradient comet; click to open a notification list with a spring-in unread count badge.

items.name: history-rail
items.title: History Rail
items.description: A form that removes the anxiety of editing, and shows its own mechanism instead of making you guess it: a labeled "Edit history" rail with a live "Checkpoint 1 of 2" readout, and a real progress ring that fills in place while you pause, so you watch a checkpoint form before it ever commits. Every 900ms pause creates a real, clickable checkpoint, not a hidden undo stack; hover a past dot for a preview before you commit to jumping, jump anywhere any time, no "discard changes?" dialog anywhere, and editing from an old checkpoint gracefully fades away the future dots it replaces instead of just erasing them.

items.name: moving-border-button
items.title: Moving Border Button
items.description: A single bright gradient segment travels the button's own rounded-rect perimeter, measured live so it fits any size.

items.name: content-card
items.title: Content Card
items.description: A clickable card for articles or case studies, with a lift-on-hover affordance.

items.name: stat-card
items.title: Stat Card
items.description: A compact metric display with a label, value, and optional delta, count-up animated on scroll. `valueSuffix`/`valueDecimals`/`deltaSuffix` cover percentages and plain counts as well as the default "k" shorthand, a negative delta renders with a real minus sign and a rose tone instead of a hardcoded plus, and the sparkline is optional rather than required.

items.name: badge
items.title: Badge
items.description: A small status pill with neutral, success, and warning tones.

items.name: pricing-card
items.title: Pricing Card
items.description: A plan card with a count-up price, a shine-swept 'popular' ribbon, and a staggered feature list.

items.name: avatar
items.title: Avatar
items.description: A single avatar with a photo-or-initials fallback, an optional online/away/offline status dot (with a soft pulse when online), and the same spring-in name/role tooltip as Avatar Group.

items.name: avatar-group
items.title: Avatar Group
items.description: An overlapping avatar stack, mixing real photos and initials fallbacks, that fans out on hover and pops a spring-in name/role tooltip; hovering the '+N' overflow indicator lists everyone it's hiding.

items.name: flip-card
items.title: Flip Card
items.description: A card that turns over on click: the front centers a circular image with a title and a muted subtitle, the back rotates to read upright with the answer, and a rotate cue sits at the bottom of each face. The default image is NASA's public-domain Magellan globe of Venus; `orientation` picks a wide or tall layout, `image` takes any src or `null`, both faces carry an sr-only instruction, and `useReducedMotion` trades the 3D spring for an instant cut. Labels, subtitle, and hint text are all props.

items.name: wave-card
items.title: Wave Card
items.description: A full-bleed teal card with an animated SVG turbulence filter tracing a caustic light net across the surface, like sunlight refracting through shallow water.

items.name: glow-card
items.title: Glow Card
items.description: A card with a large blurred gradient blob drifting slowly behind it: ambient, not cursor-tracked like Spotlight Card.

items.name: gradient-canvas
items.title: Gradient Canvas
items.description: A soft gradient surface built from colour stops, each with a drifting blur blob for depth, a grain overlay, and a live WCAG contrast readout. The band beneath is a real ARIA slider (drag, arrow keys, Shift-steps) that moves a colour along the gradient. Below that, each stop is a card whose whole face opens the library's own Color Picker; picking a colour renames the card from the hex (`Deep Indigo`, `Pale Sky`) and flips the card's own label text black or white to stay legible on the new swatch. `Add colour` blends a stop into the widest gap (two to six), presets reprint the lot. `defaultStops`, `angle`, `animated`, `onChange`, and overlaid `children` are the API; `useReducedMotion` freezes the drift.

items.name: postage-stamp
items.title: Postage Stamp
items.description: A die-cut postage frame: the perforated edge is four intersecting radial-gradient masks (real cutouts, so the drop shadow traces the scalloped edge, not a rectangle), over a grained paper surface with an inner rule, artwork window, country line, and denomination. Pass children (or upload a photo in the demo) and it prints into the window as a two-tone image; an ink prop reprints that duotone, the rule, and the value in one of four accents. Cancelled drops a multiply-blended postmark with a spring.

items.name: collection-wallet
items.title: Collection Wallet
items.description: A sleeve that holds a fanned stack of cards tucked behind its front panel, tops peeking over the lip. Drag a card up past a threshold (or click, or press Enter) and it springs clear; only one draws at a time, the label swaps to name it, and the count tracks what is in versus out. Drag it back down to file it. Generic: each item's content is any node about 160px wide; the demo fills it with Postage Stamps you can upload your own photo into, one per stamp. A tone prop recolours the sleeve.

items.name: hover-reveal-card
items.title: Hover Reveal Card
items.description: A carousel row built for text-first browsing: at rest it's only a headline and a line of description, hover or tab to it and the reveal plays in three deliberate beats rather than one flat swap, the text steps left, its photo slides in from the right a beat later, and a call-to-action arrives last once the layout has settled. Built as a real focusable control, not a hover-only trick, so keyboard users get the identical reveal on focus.

items.name: accordion
items.title: Accordion
items.description: An expandable panel with an animated height, a rotating plus-to-cross icon, and real ARIA region semantics.

items.name: testimonial-card
items.title: Testimonial Card
items.description: A quote card whose quotation-mark watermark drifts slightly with the cursor, like a subtler SpotlightCard.

items.name: pull-quote
items.title: Pull Quote
items.description: A card-less, editorial single-quote spotlight: large centered type instead of a bordered box, for the moment one quote should carry a whole section rather than sit lost inside one.

items.name: swipe-cards
items.title: Swipe Cards
items.description: A Tinder-style card stack: drag left or right to skip or save, with a tilting card, color-coded SAVE/SKIP stamps, and arrow keys as a non-drag alternative.

items.name: testimonial-carousel
items.title: Testimonial Carousel
items.description: A single-card quote carousel, distinct from Testimonial Card's static quote and Swipe Cards' skip/save stack: drag the current card left or right (or use the arrow buttons or dot pagination) to advance, with a real quotation-mark watermark and a directional slide tied to whichever way you moved.

items.name: mini-chart
items.title: Mini Chart
items.description: The same series rendered three ways off one `view` prop: a bar chart, a hand-drawn SVG line chart with a gradient fill, or a segmented radial ring built from per-value `strokeDasharray` arcs. Switching `view` crossfades between representations instead of a hard cut, and each view draws itself in on scroll rather than appearing fully formed.

items.name: region-map
items.title: Region Map
items.description: A monochrome dotted world map for dashboards, drawn on an Equal Earth projection (equal-area, full coverage: New Zealand and the Pacific are on the map, not clipped like Mercator). Land is baked to a 1-bit-per-cell base64 bitmap at three densities (`density` of `coarse`, `normal` or `fine`, 3.2k to 16.7k dots) so a small tile and a hero-sized map share one component; every dot is one colour, from eight named `variant`s (azure, ember, moss, gold, teal, iris, rose, slate) or a raw `accent`. The only variation across the map is `daylight`: pass `true` and it shades each dot by the real position of the sun (recomputed every minute) with a dashed day/night terminator and a soft glow at the sub-solar point, or pass a `Date` to pin it. `markers` are raw lat/lng with an optional pulse, `points` plots many unlabelled coordinates smaller and softer for the where-our-users-are layer, and `arcs` bow between two coordinates with a dot travelling along. `regionsOf(lat, lng)` replaces the built-in four regions with your own buckets, `regionLabels` names them for the `legend` and screen-reader controls. With `interactive`, the nearest land dot resolves a region for `onRegionHover` / `onRegionSelect`; `zoomOnSelect` flies the viewport in to frame the picked region and dims the rest, with `regionMetrics` in a floating panel and a control to fly back out. Reveal is triggered off the wrapping element, not an SVG node; full reduced-motion path drops the reveal, the arc draw-on, the fly-in, and the pulses.

export const RAW_X = 2.7066299836960748;
export const RAW_Y = 1.3173627591574133;

const A1 = 1.340264, A2 = -0.081106, A3 = 0.000893, A4 = 0.003796;
const M = Math.sqrt(3) / 2;

/**
 * Round to 1e-4 lattice units so SSR (Node) and the browser serialise the same
 * SVG coordinate. `Math.sin`/`asin`/`cos` are not bit-identical across JS
 * engines, and a 1-ULP drift in the last decimal trips React hydration.
 */
const snap = (n: number) => Math.round(n * 1e4) / 1e4;

export function projectLatLng(g: GridSpec, lat: number, lng: number): { col: number; row: number } {
  const lambda = (lng * Math.PI) / 180;
  const phi = (lat * Math.PI) / 180;
  const l = Math.asin(M * Math.sin(phi));
  const l2 = l * l;
  const l6 = l2 * l2 * l2;
  const rx = (lambda * Math.cos(l)) / (M * (A1 + 3 * A2 * l2 + l6 * (7 * A3 + 9 * A4 * l2)));
  const ry = l * (A1 + A2 * l2 + l6 * (A3 + A4 * l2));
  return {
    col: snap((rx + RAW_X) * g.scale - 0.5),
    row: snap((RAW_Y - ry) * g.scale - 0.5 - g.rowOffset),
  };
}

export function unprojectColRow(g: GridSpec, col: number, row: number): { lat: number; lng: number } {
  const x = (col + 0.5) / g.scale - RAW_X;
  const y = RAW_Y - (row + 0.5 + g.rowOffset) / g.scale;
  let l = y;
  for (let i = 0; i < 12; i++) {
    const l2 = l * l;
    const l6 = l2 * l2 * l2;
    const dl =
      (l * (A1 + A2 * l2 + l6 * (A3 + A4 * l2)) - y) /
      (A1 + 3 * A2 * l2 + l6 * (7 * A3 + 9 * A4 * l2));
    l -= dl;
    if (Math.abs(dl) < 1e-12) break;
  }
  const l2 = l * l;
  const l6 = l2 * l2 * l2;
  const lambda = (M * x * (A1 + 3 * A2 * l2 + l6 * (7 * A3 + 9 * A4 * l2))) / Math.cos(l);
  const phi = Math.asin(Math.sin(l) / M);
  return { lat: (phi * 180) / Math.PI, lng: (lambda * 180) / Math.PI };
}

export function decodeLandDots(g: GridSpec): Array<[number, number]> {
  const raw = atob(g.land);
  const dots: Array<[number, number]> = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < g.cols * g.rows; i++) {
    if (raw.charCodeAt(i >> 3) & (128 >> (i & 7))) {
      dots.push([i % g.cols, Math.floor(i / g.cols)]);
    }
  }
  return dots;
}

/** Continent-scale buckets by bounding box, checked in order. */
function classifyRegion(lat: number, lng: number): RegionId {
  if (lat >= 58 && lng >= -75 && lng <= -10) return "na"; // Greenland
  if (lat >= 12 && lng >= -170 && lng <= -52) return "na";
  if (lat < 12 && lng >= -93 && lng <= -33) return "sa";
  if (lng > 62 || lng < -140) return "apac";
  return "emea";
}

interface Dot {
  col: number;
  row: number;
  lat: number;
  lng: number;
  region: string | null;
}

/** Land dots per density, unprojected to coordinates once and cached. */
const DOT_CACHE = new Map<MapDensity, Omit<Dot, "region">[]>();
function landDots(density: MapDensity): Omit<Dot, "region">[] {
  let cached = DOT_CACHE.get(density);
  if (!cached) {
    const g = REGION_MAP_GRIDS[density];
    cached = decodeLandDots(g).map(([col, row]) => ({ col, row, ...unprojectColRow(g, col, row) }));
    DOT_CACHE.set(density, cached);
  }
  return cached;
}

const fullViewBox = (g: GridSpec) => `-2 -2 ${g.cols + 4} ${g.rows + 4}`;
const viewAspect = (g: GridSpec) => (g.cols + 4) / (g.rows + 4);

type Box = { minC: number; maxC: number; minR: number; maxR: number };

function viewBoxForBox(b: Box, ar: number, pad: number): string {
  const padX = (b.maxC - b.minC) * 0.16 + pad;
  const padY = (b.maxR - b.minR) * 0.16 + pad;
  let x = b.minC - padX;
  let y = b.minR - padY;
  let w = b.maxC - b.minC + padX * 2;
  let h = b.maxR - b.minR + padY * 2;
  if (w / h < ar) {
    const nw = h * ar;
    x -= (nw - w) / 2;
    w = nw;
  } else {
    const nh = w / ar;
    y -= (nh - h) / 2;
    h = nh;
  }
  return `${x.toFixed(2)} ${y.toFixed(2)} ${w.toFixed(2)} ${h.toFixed(2)}`;
}

function parseViewBox(s: string): [number, number, number, number] {
  const [a, b, c, d] = s.split(/\s+/).map(Number);
  return [a, b, c, d];
}

function arcPath(a: { col: number; row: number }, b: { col: number; row: number }) {
  // Round every emitted number: Math.hypot isn't bit-identical across JS engines,
  // so an unrounded `d` string drifts between SSR and the browser and breaks
  // hydration.
  const n = (v: number) => (Math.round(v * 1e3) / 1e3).toString();
  const mx = (a.col + b.col) / 2;
  const my = (a.row + b.row) / 2;
  const dist = Math.hypot(b.col - a.col, b.row - a.row);
  const lift = Math.min(dist * 0.4, 46);
  return `M ${n(a.col)} ${n(a.row)} Q ${n(mx)} ${n(my - lift)} ${n(b.col)} ${n(b.row)}`;
}

// --- solar geometry ------------------------------------------------------

const D2R = Math.PI / 180;

/**
 * Day/night is quantised into this many steps so land dots share a few paths.
 * High enough that the terminator still reads as a gradient rather than bands,
 * and the bucket count stays in the dozens either way.
 */
const DAY_STEPS = 24;

function subsolarPoint(date: Date): { lat: number; lng: number } {
  const yearStart = Date.UTC(date.getUTCFullYear(), 0, 0);
  const dayOfYear = (date.getTime() - yearStart) / 86_400_000;
  const decl = -23.44 * Math.cos(D2R * (360 / 365) * (dayOfYear + 10));
  const utcHours =
    date.getUTCHours() + date.getUTCMinutes() / 60 + date.getUTCSeconds() / 3600;
  let lng = -15 * (utcHours - 12);
  lng = (((lng + 180) % 360) + 360) % 360 - 180;
  return { lat: decl, lng };
}

function solarElevation(lat: number, lng: number, sLat: number, sLng: number): number {
  const h = (lng - sLng) * D2R;
  const s =
    Math.sin(lat * D2R) * Math.sin(sLat * D2R) +
    Math.cos(lat * D2R) * Math.cos(sLat * D2R) * Math.cos(h);
  return Math.asin(Math.max(-1, Math.min(1, s))) / D2R;
}

/** 0 at deep night, 1 in daylight, smooth through civil twilight. */
function dayFactor(elevation: number): number {
  const c = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, (elevation + 6) / 12));
  return c * c * (3 - 2 * c);
}

/** The great circle 90° from the sub-solar point, split into on-map polyline runs. */
function terminatorRuns(g: GridSpec, sLat: number, sLng: number): string[] {
  const s = [
    Math.cos(sLat * D2R) * Math.cos(sLng * D2R),
    Math.cos(sLat * D2R) * Math.sin(sLng * D2R),
    Math.sin(sLat * D2R),
  ];
  const ref = Math.abs(s[2]) < 0.9 ? [0, 0, 1] : [1, 0, 0];
  let u = [
    s[1] * ref[2] - s[2] * ref[1],
    s[2] * ref[0] - s[0] * ref[2],
    s[0] * ref[1] - s[1] * ref[0],
  ];
  const un = Math.hypot(u[0], u[1], u[2]);
  u = u.map((v) => v / un);
  const v = [
    s[1] * u[2] - s[2] * u[1],
    s[2] * u[0] - s[0] * u[2],
    s[0] * u[1] - s[1] * u[0],
  ];
  const runs: string[][] = [[]];
  let prev: [number, number] | null = null;
  for (let i = 0; i <= 240; i++) {
    const t = (i / 240) * 2 * Math.PI;
    const ct = Math.cos(t);
    const st = Math.sin(t);
    const p = [ct * u[0] + st * v[0], ct * u[1] + st * v[1], ct * u[2] + st * v[2]];
    const lat = Math.asin(p[2]) / D2R;
    const lng = Math.atan2(p[1], p[0]) / D2R;
    const { col, row } = projectLatLng(g, lat, lng);
    if (prev && Math.hypot(col - prev[0], row - prev[1]) > g.cols * 0.1) runs.push([]);
    runs[runs.length - 1].push(`${col.toFixed(1)},${row.toFixed(1)}`);
    prev = [col, row];
  }
  return runs.filter((r) => r.length > 1).map((r) => r.join(" "));
}

export function RegionMap({
  variant = "azure",
  accent,
  density = "normal",
  daylight = false,
  terminator: showTerminator,
  selectedRegion = null,
  markers = [],
  arcs = [],
  points = [],
  pointRadius,
  regionsOf,
  regionLabels,
  legend = false,
  zoomOnSelect = false,
  regionMetrics,
  interactive = false,
  onRegionHover,
  onRegionSelect,
  animate = true,
  dotRadius,
  className = "text-slate-500",
  "aria-label": ariaLabel = "World map",
}: RegionMapProps) {
  const grid = REGION_MAP_GRIDS[density] ?? REGION_MAP_GRIDS.normal;
  // Dots, markers and strokes are sized in grid units, so they scale with density.
  const unit = grid.cols / 256;
  const r = dotRadius ?? 0.62 * unit;
  const uid = useId().replace(/:/g, "");
  const rootRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const svgRef = useRef<SVGSVGElement>(null);
  const reduceMotion = useReducedMotion();
  const play = animate && !reduceMotion;
  const inView = useInView(rootRef, { once: true, margin: "-10% 0px" });
  const revealed = !play || inView;
  const [hovered, setHovered] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [focused, setFocused] = useState<string | null>(null);

  const tone = accent ?? VARIANTS[variant] ?? VARIANTS.azure;
  const drawTerminator = showTerminator ?? Boolean(daylight);

  // Live clock for `daylight === true`, set after mount so SSR and the client agree.
  const [liveNow, setLiveNow] = useState<Date | null>(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (daylight !== true) return;
    const raf = requestAnimationFrame(() => setLiveNow(new Date()));
    const id = setInterval(() => setLiveNow(new Date()), 60_000);
    return () => {
      cancelAnimationFrame(raf);
      clearInterval(id);
    };
  }, [daylight]);

  const now = daylight instanceof Date ? daylight : daylight ? liveNow : null;
  const sun = useMemo(() => (now ? subsolarPoint(now) : null), [now]);

  const lightByDot = useMemo(() => {
    if (!sun) return null;
    return landDots(density).map((d) =>
      dayFactor(solarElevation(d.lat, d.lng, sun.lat, sun.lng)),
    );
  }, [sun, density]);

  const dots = useMemo<Dot[]>(
    () =>
      landDots(density).map((d) => ({
        ...d,
        region: regionsOf ? regionsOf(d.lat, d.lng) : classifyRegion(d.lat, d.lng),
      })),
    [regionsOf, density],
  );

  /** Lattice cell to index into `dots`, so pointer hit-testing is a local lookup. */
  const dotIndex = useMemo(() => {
    const idx = new Int32Array(grid.cols * grid.rows).fill(-1);
    for (let i = 0; i < dots.length; i++) idx[dots[i].row * grid.cols + dots[i].col] = i;
    return idx;
  }, [dots, grid.cols, grid.rows]);

  /** Per-dot path geometry never changes, so build the segments once. */
  const dotSegs = useMemo(() => dots.map((d) => `M${d.col} ${d.row}h0`), [dots]);

  // Every land dot is the same size, so they are drawn as zero-length subpaths
  // (`M x y h0` with a round linecap) grouped by fill and opacity, rather than
  // one <circle> each. A hover used to re-render every circle in the map; now it
  // rewrites a couple of dozen `d` strings.
  const landPaths = useMemo(() => {
    const buckets = new Map<string, { fill: string; opacity: number; parts: string[] }>();
    for (let i = 0; i < dots.length; i++) {
      const { fill, opacity } = fillFor(dots[i], i);
      const key = `${fill}|${opacity.toFixed(3)}`;
      let bucket = buckets.get(key);
      if (!bucket) buckets.set(key, (bucket = { fill, opacity, parts: [] }));
      bucket.parts.push(dotSegs[i]);
    }
    return [...buckets].map(([key, b]) => ({ key, d: b.parts.join(""), fill: b.fill, opacity: b.opacity }));
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [dots, dotSegs, lightByDot, tone, hovered, focused, selectedRegion]);

  const regionBoxes = useMemo(() => {
    const acc = new Map<string, { cols: number[]; rows: number[] }>();
    for (const d of dots) {
      if (d.region == null) continue;
      let e = acc.get(d.region);
      if (!e) acc.set(d.region, (e = { cols: [], rows: [] }));
      e.cols.push(d.col);
      e.rows.push(d.row);
    }
    const q = (arr: number[], t: number) =>
      arr[Math.min(arr.length - 1, Math.max(0, Math.round(t * (arr.length - 1))))];
    const m = new Map<string, Box>();
    for (const [region, { cols, rows }] of acc) {
      cols.sort((a, b) => a - b);
      rows.sort((a, b) => a - b);
      m.set(region, {
        minC: q(cols, 0.02),
        maxC: q(cols, 0.98),
        minR: q(rows, 0.02),
        maxR: q(rows, 0.98),
      });
    }
    return m;
  }, [dots]);

  // Animate the viewBox by lerping its four numbers off a spring-driven 0..1.
  const full = fullViewBox(grid);
  const viewBox = useMotionValue(full);
  useMotionValueEvent(viewBox, "change", (v) => svgRef.current?.setAttribute("viewBox", v));
  const targetViewBox = useMemo(() => {
    if (!focused) return full;
    const b = regionBoxes.get(focused);
    return b ? viewBoxForBox(b, viewAspect(grid), 6 * unit) : full;
  }, [focused, regionBoxes, full, grid, unit]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (reduceMotion) {
      viewBox.set(targetViewBox);
      return;
    }
    const from = parseViewBox(viewBox.get());
    const to = parseViewBox(targetViewBox);
    const controls = tween(0, 1, {
      type: "spring",
      stiffness: 150,
      damping: 26,
      onUpdate: (p) => {
        viewBox.set(from.map((f, k) => (f + (to[k] - f) * p).toFixed(2)).join(" "));
      },
    });
    return () => controls.stop();
  }, [targetViewBox, reduceMotion, viewBox]);

  const labels = regionLabels ?? DEFAULT_REGION_LABELS;
  const legendRegions = regionLabels
    ? Object.keys(regionLabels)
    : Object.keys(DEFAULT_REGION_LABELS);

  function fillFor(d: Dot, i: number): { fill: string; opacity: number } {
    // Quantised so dots collapse into a handful of shared buckets below.
    const dayF = lightByDot ? Math.round(lightByDot[i] * (DAY_STEPS - 1)) / (DAY_STEPS - 1) : 1;
    // Night is a colour shift toward --map-night, not a fade. Fading toward the
    // background only reads as darkness on a dark surface; on a light one the
    // night hemisphere simply disappears. Mixing keeps every land dot present
    // in both themes and leaves the opacity channel free for selection state.
    const fill = lightByDot
      ? `color-mix(in srgb, ${tone} ${Math.round(26 + 74 * dayF)}%, var(--map-night))`
      : tone;
    const isActive =
      d.region != null && (d.region === selectedRegion || d.region === hovered || d.region === focused);
    const dim = focused && d.region !== focused ? 0.22 : 1;
    return { fill, opacity: (isActive ? 1 : 0.86) * dim };
  }

  function pointerRegion(e: { clientX: number; clientY: number }): string | null {
    const svg = svgRef.current;
    if (!svg) return null;
    const ctm = svg.getScreenCTM();
    if (!ctm) return null;
    const pt = new DOMPoint(e.clientX, e.clientY).matrixTransform(ctm.inverse());
    // Dots sit on an integer lattice, so only the cells within the hit radius
    // can win. Scanning all of them cost ~45ms per pointermove, which a mouse
    // fires often enough to saturate the main thread.
    const reach = 5 * unit;
    const span = Math.ceil(reach);
    const c0 = Math.round(pt.x);
    const r0 = Math.round(pt.y);
    let best: Dot | null = null;
    let bestD = reach * reach;
    for (let dr = -span; dr <= span; dr++) {
      const row = r0 + dr;
      if (row < 0 || row >= grid.rows) continue;
      for (let dc = -span; dc <= span; dc++) {
        const col = c0 + dc;
        if (col < 0 || col >= grid.cols) continue;
        const i = dotIndex[row * grid.cols + col];
        if (i < 0) continue;
        const d = dots[i];
        if (d.region == null) continue;
        const dd = (d.col - pt.x) ** 2 + (d.row - pt.y) ** 2;
        if (dd < bestD) {
          bestD = dd;
          best = d;
        }
      }
    }
    return best ? best.region : null;
  }

  function setHover(region: string | null) {
    setHovered((prev) => {
      if (prev !== region) onRegionHover?.(region);
      return region;
    });
  }

  function selectRegion(region: string) {
    onRegionSelect?.(region);
    if (zoomOnSelect) setFocused((cur) => (cur === region ? null : region));
  }

  const projected = markers.map((m) => ({ ...m, ...projectLatLng(grid, m.lat, m.lng) }));
  const plotted = useMemo(
    () => points.map((p, i) => ({ key: p.id ?? i, ...projectLatLng(grid, p.lat, p.lng) })),
    [points, grid],
  );
  const sunAt = sun ? projectLatLng(grid, sun.lat, sun.lng) : null;
  const runs = useMemo(
    () => (sun && drawTerminator ? terminatorRuns(grid, sun.lat, sun.lng) : null),
    [sun, drawTerminator, grid],
  );
  const panel = focused ? regionMetrics?.[focused] : undefined;

  return (
    // The sun glow is the one colour that cannot serve both themes: a pale
    // cream reads as warm light on a dark map and disappears on a white one.
    // It is set as a CSS variable so the consumer's own dark-mode strategy
    // drives it, with no theme detection in JS and nothing to mismatch on hydration.
    <div
      ref={rootRef}
      className={`[--map-night:#64748b] [--map-sun:#d97706] dark:[--map-night:#334155] dark:[--map-sun:#fde6b4] ${className}`}
    >
      <div className="relative">
        <svg
          ref={svgRef}
          viewBox={full}
          className="w-full select-none"
          role="img"
          aria-label={ariaLabel}
          onPointerMove={interactive ? (e) => setHover(pointerRegion(e)) : undefined}
          onPointerLeave={interactive ? () => setHover(null) : undefined}
          onClick={
            interactive
              ? (e) => {
                  const r = pointerRegion(e);
                  if (r) selectRegion(r);
                }
              : undefined
          }
        >
          <defs>
            <radialGradient id={`${uid}-pulse`}>
              <stop offset="0%" stopColor={tone} stopOpacity="0.5" />
              <stop offset="100%" stopColor={tone} stopOpacity="0" />
            </radialGradient>
            <radialGradient id={`${uid}-sun`}>
              {/* style, not an attribute: var() only resolves in a CSS declaration. */}
              <stop offset="0%" style={{ stopColor: "var(--map-sun)", stopOpacity: 0.26 }} />
              <stop offset="100%" style={{ stopColor: "var(--map-sun)", stopOpacity: 0 }} />
            </radialGradient>
          </defs>

          {sunAt && (
            <circle
              cx={sunAt.col}
              cy={sunAt.row}
              r={24 * unit}
              fill={`url(#${uid}-sun)`}
              pointerEvents="none"
            />
          )}

          <g
            style={{
              opacity: revealed ? 1 : 0,
              transition: play ? "opacity 1.1s ease" : undefined,
            }}
          >
            {landPaths.map((b) => (
              <path
                key={b.key}
                d={b.d}
                fill="none"
                strokeWidth={r * 2}
                strokeLinecap="round"
                style={{ stroke: b.fill, strokeOpacity: b.opacity }}
              />
            ))}
          </g>

          {runs?.map((pts, i) => (
            <polyline
              key={i}
              points={pts}
              fill="none"
              stroke={tone}
              strokeWidth={1}
              strokeOpacity={0.4}
              strokeDasharray="2.5 2.5"
              strokeLinecap="round"
              vectorEffect="non-scaling-stroke"
            />
          ))}

          {arcs.map((arc) => {
            const a = projectLatLng(grid, arc.from[0], arc.from[1]);
            const b = projectLatLng(grid, arc.to[0], arc.to[1]);
            const d = arcPath(a, b);
            return (
              <g key={arc.id}>
                <motion.path
                  d={d}
                  fill="none"
                  stroke={tone}
                  strokeWidth={0.9}
                  strokeOpacity={0.6}
                  strokeLinecap="round"
                  vectorEffect="non-scaling-stroke"
                  initial={false}
                  animate={{ pathLength: revealed ? 1 : 0 }}
                  transition={{ duration: play ? 1.1 : 0, ease: [0.22, 1, 0.36, 1] }}
                />
                {play && revealed && (
                  <motion.circle
                    r={1.3 * unit}
                    fill={tone}
                    animate={{ offsetDistance: "100%" }}
                    transition={{ duration: 2.4, repeat: Infinity, ease: "easeInOut", repeatDelay: 0.6 }}
                    style={{ offsetPath: `path("${d}")`, offsetDistance: "0%" }}
                  />
                )}
              </g>
            );
          })}

          {projected.map((m) => (
            <g key={m.id}>
              {m.pulse && play && revealed && (
                <motion.circle
                  cx={m.col}
                  cy={m.row}
                  r={6 * unit}
                  fill={`url(#${uid}-pulse)`}
                  initial={{ scale: 0.4, opacity: 0.8 }}
                  animate={{ scale: 1.6, opacity: 0 }}
                  transition={{ duration: 2, repeat: Infinity, ease: "easeOut" }}
                  style={{ transformOrigin: `${m.col}px ${m.row}px` }}
                />
              )}
              <circle cx={m.col} cy={m.row} r={2 * unit} fill={tone} />
              <circle
                cx={m.col}
                cy={m.row}
                r={2 * unit}
                fill="none"
                stroke={tone}
                strokeOpacity={0.35}
                strokeWidth={1.4}
                vectorEffect="non-scaling-stroke"
              />
              {m.label && !focused && (
                <text
                  x={m.col + 3.5 * unit}
                  y={m.row + 1.4 * unit}
                  fill="currentColor"
                  style={{ fontFamily: "inherit", fontWeight: 600, fontSize: 5 * unit }}
                >
                  {m.label}
                </text>
              )}
            </g>
          ))}

          {plotted.map((p) => (
            <circle
              key={p.key}
              cx={p.col}
              cy={p.row}
              r={pointRadius ?? 1.1 * unit}
              fill={tone}
              opacity={0.85}
            />
          ))}
        </svg>

        {focused && (
          <button
            type="button"
            onClick={() => setFocused(null)}
            className="absolute left-3 top-3 rounded-md border border-slate-200 bg-white/80 px-2 py-1 text-xs text-slate-700 shadow-sm backdrop-blur transition-colors hover:bg-white dark:border-white/15 dark:bg-slate-950/70 dark:text-slate-200 dark:shadow-none dark:hover:bg-slate-950/90"
          >
            {"←"} All regions
          </button>
        )}

        {panel && (
          <div className="absolute right-3 top-3 min-w-[9rem] rounded-lg border border-slate-200 bg-white/85 px-3 py-2 text-slate-700 shadow-sm backdrop-blur dark:border-white/10 dark:bg-slate-950/80 dark:text-slate-200 dark:shadow-none">
            <p className="text-sm font-medium">{labels[focused as string] ?? focused}</p>
            <dl className="mt-2 space-y-1">
              {panel.map((m) => (
                <div key={m.label} className="flex items-baseline justify-between gap-4 text-xs">
                  <dt className="opacity-55">{m.label}</dt>
                  <dd className="tabular-nums">{m.value}</dd>
                </div>
              ))}
            </dl>
          </div>
        )}
      </div>

      {legend && (
        <ul className="mt-4 flex flex-wrap gap-x-4 gap-y-2 text-xs text-current">
          {legendRegions.map((r) => {
            const item = (
              <>
                <span
                  aria-hidden
                  className="inline-block h-2.5 w-2.5 shrink-0 rounded-[3px]"
                  style={{
                    backgroundColor: tone,
                    opacity: r === (focused ?? selectedRegion) ? 1 : 0.55,
                  }}
                />
                <span className="opacity-90">{labels[r] ?? r}</span>
              </>
            );
            return (
              <li key={r}>
                {interactive ? (
                  <button
                    type="button"
                    onClick={() => selectRegion(r)}
                    onFocus={() => setHover(r)}
                    onBlur={() => setHover(null)}
                    onMouseEnter={() => setHover(r)}
                    onMouseLeave={() => setHover(null)}
                    className="flex items-center gap-2 rounded-md px-1 py-0.5 outline-offset-2 transition-colors hover:bg-slate-500/10 focus-visible:outline focus-visible:outline-2"
                    aria-pressed={r === (focused ?? selectedRegion)}
                  >
                    {item}
                  </button>
                ) : (
                  <span className="flex items-center gap-2 px-1 py-0.5">{item}</span>
                )}
              </li>
            );
          })}
        </ul>
      )}

      {interactive && !legend && (
        <div className="sr-only">
          {legendRegions.map((r) => (
            <button key={r} type="button" onFocus={() => setHover(r)} onBlur={() => setHover(null)} onClick={() => selectRegion(r)}>
              {labels[r] ?? r}
            </button>
          ))}
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

items.name: globe-map
items.title: Globe Map
items.description: The orthographic sibling of Region Map: the same baked Equal Earth land bitmap, unprojected back to coordinates and re-projected onto a sphere. Because Equal Earth is equal-area, that grid is already a uniform sampling of the globe, so no second dataset is needed. Drag it to spin, with inertia on release and arrow-key control for keyboards; `autoRotate` sets an idle spin in degrees per second, `centerOn={[lat, lng]}` springs a named view into place taking the short way around the meridian, and all three drivers write one shared centre so grabbing the globe mid-flight simply takes over. Rotating that many dots through React would crawl, so the land is drawn as zero-length subpaths bucketed into 16 opacity steps, which turns a per-frame rebuild of the sphere into 16 path strings instead of thousands of elements (measured at about four times the frame rate of one circle per dot). The far hemisphere is culled by the sign of the view dot product, and dots fade toward the limb so the sphere reads as curved. `arcs` are true great circles interpolated on the sphere and split wherever they round the edge, not screen-space beziers. `daylight` shades each dot by the real sun position with the terminator drawn as the great circle 90 degrees from it, `graticule` adds meridians and parallels, `points` plots many unlabelled coordinates, and `markers` take an optional pulse and label. Eight colour variants or a raw `accent`; `density` trades dot count against rotation cost, holding 60fps at coarse and normal while fine is better kept for a globe that sits still.

items.name: us-map
items.title: US State Map
items.description: The same dotted-map treatment at country scale: the contiguous United States on a single Albers conic equal-area cone, with every land dot tagged with the state that contains it. d3 ships a composite geoAlbersUsa that stitches three cones together with region tests, which is far too much code to inline into a copy-paste file, so one cone is used instead and its forward and inverse are about a dozen lines each, which keeps `markers`, `arcs` and `points` placeable by raw lat/lng. State membership is baked from real polygon containment, not bounding boxes: 13,411 dots across 48 states, stored as a 1-bit land bitmap plus one palette byte per dot. Hovering hit-tests the nearest dot to name a state, `zoomOnSelect` flies the viewport in to frame it and dims the rest, and `stateMetrics` fills a floating panel. Monochrome, with eight colour variants or a raw `accent`, and the same live `daylight` shading sweeping across the country. Alaska and Hawai'i sit outside this cone and are not drawn.

  useMotionValueEvent,
  useReducedMotion,
} from "framer-motion";

export const US_MAP_COLS = 208;
export const US_MAP_ROWS = 129;

export const US_MAP_PROJECTION = {
  cols: 208,
  rows: 129,
  scale: 264.192169690252,
  xMin: -0.41725127961093395,
  yMax: 0.2590562322432044,
} as const;

const D2R = Math.PI / 180;
const N = 0.6028370046288244;
const C = 1.351221325417899;
const RHO0 = 1.3032624269880215;
const LAM0 = -1.6755160819145565;

export function projectUs(lat: number, lng: number): { col: number; row: number } {
  const { scale, xMin, yMax } = US_MAP_PROJECTION;
  const rho = Math.sqrt(C - 2 * N * Math.sin(lat * D2R)) / N;
  const theta = N * (lng * D2R - LAM0);
  const x = rho * Math.sin(theta);
  const y = RHO0 - rho * Math.cos(theta);
  return { col: (x - xMin) * scale - 0.5, row: (yMax - y) * scale - 0.5 };
}

export function unprojectUs(col: number, row: number): { lat: number; lng: number } {
  const { scale, xMin, yMax } = US_MAP_PROJECTION;
  const x = xMin + (col + 0.5) / scale;
  const y = yMax - (row + 0.5) / scale;
  const dy = RHO0 - y;
  const rho = Math.sqrt(x * x + dy * dy) * (N < 0 ? -1 : 1);
  const theta = Math.atan2(x, dy);
  return {
    lat: Math.asin(Math.max(-1, Math.min(1, (C - rho * rho * N * N) / (2 * N)))) / D2R,
    lng: (LAM0 + theta / N) / D2R,

}

export function decodeUsDots(): UsDot[] {
  const landRaw = atob(US_MAP_LAND_B64);
  const stateRaw = atob(US_MAP_STATES_B64);
  const dots: UsDot[] = [];
  let d = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < US_MAP_COLS * US_MAP_ROWS; i++) {
    if (landRaw.charCodeAt(i >> 3) & (128 >> (i & 7))) {
      dots.push({
        col: i % US_MAP_COLS,
        row: Math.floor(i / US_MAP_COLS),
        state: STATE_NAMES[stateRaw.charCodeAt(d++)],
      });
    }
  }
  return dots;
}

/**
 * Day/night is quantised into this many steps so land dots share a few paths.
 * High enough that the terminator still reads as a gradient rather than bands,
 * and the bucket count stays in the dozens either way.
 */
const DAY_STEPS = 24;

interface Dot extends UsDot {
  lat: number;
  lng: number;
}

let DOTS: Dot[] | null = null;
function usDots(): Dot[] {
  if (!DOTS) {
    DOTS = decodeUsDots().map((d) => ({ ...d, ...unprojectUs(d.col, d.row) }));
  }
  return DOTS;
}

const FULL_VIEWBOX = `-3 -3 ${US_MAP_COLS + 6} ${US_MAP_ROWS + 6}`;
const VIEW_AR = (US_MAP_COLS + 6) / (US_MAP_ROWS + 6);

type Box = { minC: number; maxC: number; minR: number; maxR: number };

function viewBoxForBox(b: Box): string {
  const padX = (b.maxC - b.minC) * 0.2 + 5;
  const padY = (b.maxR - b.minR) * 0.2 + 5;
  let x = b.minC - padX;
  let y = b.minR - padY;
  let w = b.maxC - b.minC + padX * 2;
  let h = b.maxR - b.minR + padY * 2;
  if (w / h < VIEW_AR) {
    const nw = h * VIEW_AR;
    x -= (nw - w) / 2;
    w = nw;
  } else {
    const nh = w / VIEW_AR;
    y -= (nh - h) / 2;
    h = nh;
  }
  return `${x.toFixed(2)} ${y.toFixed(2)} ${w.toFixed(2)} ${h.toFixed(2)}`;
}

function parseViewBox(s: string): [number, number, number, number] {
  const [a, b, c, d] = s.split(/\s+/).map(Number);
  return [a, b, c, d];
}

function arcPath(a: { col: number; row: number }, b: { col: number; row: number }) {
  const mx = (a.col + b.col) / 2;
  const my = (a.row + b.row) / 2;
  const lift = Math.min(Math.hypot(b.col - a.col, b.row - a.row) * 0.35, 30);
  return `M ${a.col} ${a.row} Q ${mx} ${my - lift} ${b.col} ${b.row}`;
}

// --- solar geometry ------------------------------------------------------

function subsolarPoint(date: Date): { lat: number; lng: number } {
  const yearStart = Date.UTC(date.getUTCFullYear(), 0, 0);
  const dayOfYear = (date.getTime() - yearStart) / 86_400_000;
  const decl = -23.44 * Math.cos(D2R * (360 / 365) * (dayOfYear + 10));
  const utcHours =
    date.getUTCHours() + date.getUTCMinutes() / 60 + date.getUTCSeconds() / 3600;
  let lng = -15 * (utcHours - 12);
  lng = (((lng + 180) % 360) + 360) % 360 - 180;
  return { lat: decl, lng };
}

function solarElevation(lat: number, lng: number, sLat: number, sLng: number): number {
  const h = (lng - sLng) * D2R;
  const s =
    Math.sin(lat * D2R) * Math.sin(sLat * D2R) +
    Math.cos(lat * D2R) * Math.cos(sLat * D2R) * Math.cos(h);
  return Math.asin(Math.max(-1, Math.min(1, s))) / D2R;
}

function dayFactor(elevation: number): number {
  const c = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, (elevation + 6) / 12));
  return c * c * (3 - 2 * c);
}
