export function UsMap({
  variant = "azure",
  accent,
  daylight = false,
  selectedState = null,
  markers = [],
  arcs = [],
  points = [],
  pointRadius,
  zoomOnSelect = false,
  stateMetrics,
  interactive = false,
  onStateHover,
  onStateSelect,
  animate = true,
  dotRadius = 0.4,
  className = "text-slate-500",
  "aria-label": ariaLabel = "Map of the contiguous United States",
}: UsMapProps) {
  const uid = useId().replace(/:/g, "");
  const rootRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const svgRef = useRef<SVGSVGElement>(null);
  const reduceMotion = useReducedMotion();
  const play = animate && !reduceMotion;
  const inView = useInView(rootRef, { once: true, margin: "-10% 0px" });
  const revealed = !play || inView;
  const [hovered, setHovered] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [focused, setFocused] = useState<string | null>(null);

  const tone = accent ?? VARIANTS[variant] ?? VARIANTS.azure;
  const dots = usDots();

  // Live clock for `daylight === true`, set after mount so SSR and the client agree.
  const [liveNow, setLiveNow] = useState<Date | null>(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (daylight !== true) return;
    const raf = requestAnimationFrame(() => setLiveNow(new Date()));
    const id = setInterval(() => setLiveNow(new Date()), 60_000);
    return () => {
      cancelAnimationFrame(raf);
      clearInterval(id);
    };
  }, [daylight]);

  const now = daylight instanceof Date ? daylight : daylight ? liveNow : null;
  const sun = useMemo(() => (now ? subsolarPoint(now) : null), [now]);

  const lightByDot = useMemo(() => {
    if (!sun) return null;
    return dots.map((d) => dayFactor(solarElevation(d.lat, d.lng, sun.lat, sun.lng)));
  }, [sun, dots]);

  /** Lattice cell to index into `dots`, so pointer hit-testing is a local lookup. */
  const dotIndex = useMemo(() => {
    const idx = new Int32Array(US_MAP_COLS * US_MAP_ROWS).fill(-1);
    for (let i = 0; i < dots.length; i++) idx[dots[i].row * US_MAP_COLS + dots[i].col] = i;
    return idx;
  }, [dots]);

  /** Per-dot path geometry never changes, so build the segments once. */
  const dotSegs = useMemo(() => dots.map((d) => `M${d.col} ${d.row}h0`), [dots]);

  // Every land dot is the same size, so they are drawn as zero-length subpaths
  // (`M x y h0` with a round linecap) grouped by fill and opacity, rather than
  // one <circle> each. A hover used to re-render all 13,411 circles; now it
  // rewrites a couple of dozen `d` strings.
  const landPaths = useMemo(() => {
    const buckets = new Map<string, { fill: string; opacity: number; parts: string[] }>();
    for (let i = 0; i < dots.length; i++) {
      const { fill, opacity } = fillFor(dots[i], i);
      const key = `${fill}|${opacity.toFixed(3)}`;
      let bucket = buckets.get(key);
      if (!bucket) buckets.set(key, (bucket = { fill, opacity, parts: [] }));
      bucket.parts.push(dotSegs[i]);
    }
    return [...buckets].map(([key, b]) => ({ key, d: b.parts.join(""), fill: b.fill, opacity: b.opacity }));
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [dots, dotSegs, lightByDot, tone, hovered, focused, selectedState]);

  const stateBoxes = useMemo(() => {
    const m = new Map<string, Box>();
    for (const d of dots) {
      const b = m.get(d.state);
      if (!b) m.set(d.state, { minC: d.col, maxC: d.col, minR: d.row, maxR: d.row });
      else {
        b.minC = Math.min(b.minC, d.col);
        b.maxC = Math.max(b.maxC, d.col);
        b.minR = Math.min(b.minR, d.row);
        b.maxR = Math.max(b.maxR, d.row);
      }
    }
    return m;
  }, [dots]);

  // Animate the viewBox by lerping its four numbers off a spring-driven 0..1.
  const viewBox = useMotionValue(FULL_VIEWBOX);
  useMotionValueEvent(viewBox, "change", (v) => svgRef.current?.setAttribute("viewBox", v));
  const targetViewBox = useMemo(() => {
    if (!focused) return FULL_VIEWBOX;
    const b = stateBoxes.get(focused);
    return b ? viewBoxForBox(b) : FULL_VIEWBOX;
  }, [focused, stateBoxes]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (reduceMotion) {
      viewBox.set(targetViewBox);
      return;
    }
    const from = parseViewBox(viewBox.get());
    const to = parseViewBox(targetViewBox);
    const controls = tween(0, 1, {
      type: "spring",
      stiffness: 150,
      damping: 26,
      onUpdate: (p) => {
        viewBox.set(from.map((f, k) => (f + (to[k] - f) * p).toFixed(2)).join(" "));
      },
    });
    return () => controls.stop();
  }, [targetViewBox, reduceMotion, viewBox]);

  function fillFor(d: Dot, i: number): { fill: string; opacity: number } {
    // Quantised so dots collapse into a handful of shared buckets below.
    const dayF = lightByDot ? Math.round(lightByDot[i] * (DAY_STEPS - 1)) / (DAY_STEPS - 1) : 1;
    // Night is a colour shift toward --map-night, not a fade. Fading toward the
    // background only reads as darkness on a dark surface; on a light one the
    // night side simply disappears. Mixing keeps every land dot present in both
    // themes and leaves the opacity channel free for selection state.
    const fill = lightByDot
      ? `color-mix(in srgb, ${tone} ${Math.round(26 + 74 * dayF)}%, var(--map-night))`
      : tone;
    const isActive = d.state === selectedState || d.state === hovered || d.state === focused;
    const dim = focused && d.state !== focused ? 0.2 : 1;
    return { fill, opacity: (isActive ? 1 : 0.86) * dim };
  }

  function pointerState(e: { clientX: number; clientY: number }): string | null {
    const svg = svgRef.current;
    if (!svg) return null;
    const ctm = svg.getScreenCTM();
    if (!ctm) return null;
    const pt = new DOMPoint(e.clientX, e.clientY).matrixTransform(ctm.inverse());
    // Dots sit on an integer lattice, so only the cells within the hit radius
    // can win. Scanning all 13,411 cost ~42ms per pointermove, which a mouse
    // fires often enough to saturate the main thread.
    const span = 5;
    const c0 = Math.round(pt.x);
    const r0 = Math.round(pt.y);
    let best: Dot | null = null;
    let bestD = 20;
    for (let dr = -span; dr <= span; dr++) {
      const row = r0 + dr;
      if (row < 0 || row >= US_MAP_ROWS) continue;
      for (let dc = -span; dc <= span; dc++) {
        const col = c0 + dc;
        if (col < 0 || col >= US_MAP_COLS) continue;
        const i = dotIndex[row * US_MAP_COLS + col];
        if (i < 0) continue;
        const d = dots[i];
        const dd = (d.col - pt.x) ** 2 + (d.row - pt.y) ** 2;
        if (dd < bestD) {
          bestD = dd;
          best = d;
        }
      }
    }
    return best ? best.state : null;
  }

  function setHover(state: string | null) {
    setHovered((prev) => {
      if (prev !== state) onStateHover?.(state);
      return state;
    });
  }

  function selectState(state: string) {
    onStateSelect?.(state);
    if (zoomOnSelect) setFocused((cur) => (cur === state ? null : state));
  }

  const projected = markers.map((m) => ({ ...m, ...projectUs(m.lat, m.lng) }));
  const plotted = useMemo(
    () => points.map((p, i) => ({ key: p.id ?? i, ...projectUs(p.lat, p.lng) })),
    [points],
  );
  const panel = focused ? stateMetrics?.[focused] : undefined;

  return (
    // --map-night is the colour the land shifts toward at night; it is a CSS
    // variable so the consumer's own dark-mode strategy drives it, with no
    // theme detection in JS and nothing to mismatch on hydration.
    <div
      ref={rootRef}
      className={`[--map-night:#64748b] dark:[--map-night:#334155] ${className}`}
    >
      <div className="relative">
        <svg
          ref={svgRef}
          viewBox={FULL_VIEWBOX}
          className="w-full select-none"
          role="img"
          aria-label={ariaLabel}
          onPointerMove={interactive ? (e) => setHover(pointerState(e)) : undefined}
          onPointerLeave={interactive ? () => setHover(null) : undefined}
          onClick={
            interactive
              ? (e) => {
                  const s = pointerState(e);
                  if (s) selectState(s);
                }
              : undefined
          }
        >
          <defs>
            <radialGradient id={`${uid}-pulse`}>
              <stop offset="0%" stopColor={tone} stopOpacity="0.5" />
              <stop offset="100%" stopColor={tone} stopOpacity="0" />
            </radialGradient>
          </defs>

          <g
            style={{
              opacity: revealed ? 1 : 0,
              transition: play ? "opacity 1.1s ease" : undefined,
            }}
          >
            {landPaths.map((b) => (
              <path
                key={b.key}
                d={b.d}
                fill="none"
                strokeWidth={dotRadius * 2}
                strokeLinecap="round"
                style={{ stroke: b.fill, strokeOpacity: b.opacity }}
              />
            ))}
          </g>

          {arcs.map((arc) => {
            const a = projectUs(arc.from[0], arc.from[1]);
            const b = projectUs(arc.to[0], arc.to[1]);
            const d = arcPath(a, b);
            return (
              <motion.path
                key={arc.id}
                d={d}
                fill="none"
                stroke={tone}
                strokeWidth={0.9}
                strokeOpacity={0.6}
                strokeLinecap="round"
                vectorEffect="non-scaling-stroke"
                initial={false}
                animate={{ pathLength: revealed ? 1 : 0 }}
                transition={{ duration: play ? 1.1 : 0, ease: [0.22, 1, 0.36, 1] }}
              />
            );
          })}

          {plotted.map((p) => (
            <circle
              key={p.key}
              cx={p.col}
              cy={p.row}
              r={pointRadius ?? 1}
              fill={tone}
              opacity={0.85}
            />
          ))}

          {projected.map((m) => (
            <g key={m.id}>
              {m.pulse && play && revealed && (
                <motion.circle
                  cx={m.col}
                  cy={m.row}
                  r={5}
                  fill={`url(#${uid}-pulse)`}
                  initial={{ scale: 0.4, opacity: 0.8 }}
                  animate={{ scale: 1.6, opacity: 0 }}
                  transition={{ duration: 2, repeat: Infinity, ease: "easeOut" }}
                  style={{ transformOrigin: `${m.col}px ${m.row}px` }}
                />
              )}
              <circle cx={m.col} cy={m.row} r={1.8} fill={tone} />
              <circle
                cx={m.col}
                cy={m.row}
                r={1.8}
                fill="none"
                stroke={tone}
                strokeOpacity={0.4}
                strokeWidth={1.2}
                vectorEffect="non-scaling-stroke"
              />
              {m.label && !focused && (
                <text
                  x={m.col + 3}
                  y={m.row + 1.2}
                  fill="currentColor"
                  style={{ fontFamily: "inherit", fontWeight: 600, fontSize: 4.5 }}
                >
                  {m.label}
                </text>
              )}
            </g>
          ))}
        </svg>

        {focused && (
          <button
            type="button"
            onClick={() => setFocused(null)}
            className="absolute left-3 top-3 rounded-md border border-slate-200 bg-white/80 px-2 py-1 text-xs text-slate-700 shadow-sm backdrop-blur transition-colors hover:bg-white dark:border-white/15 dark:bg-slate-950/70 dark:text-slate-200 dark:shadow-none dark:hover:bg-slate-950/90"
          >
            {"←"} All states
          </button>
        )}

        {panel && (
          <div className="absolute right-3 top-3 min-w-[9rem] rounded-lg border border-slate-200 bg-white/85 px-3 py-2 text-slate-700 shadow-sm backdrop-blur dark:border-white/10 dark:bg-slate-950/80 dark:text-slate-200 dark:shadow-none">
            <p className="text-sm font-medium">{focused}</p>
            <dl className="mt-2 space-y-1">
              {panel.map((m) => (
                <div key={m.label} className="flex items-baseline justify-between gap-4 text-xs">
                  <dt className="opacity-55">{m.label}</dt>
                  <dd className="tabular-nums">{m.value}</dd>
                </div>
              ))}
            </dl>
          </div>
        )}
      </div>

      {interactive && (
        <div className="sr-only">
          {STATE_NAMES.map((s) => (
            <button
              key={s}
              type="button"
              onFocus={() => setHover(s)}
              onBlur={() => setHover(null)}
              onClick={() => selectState(s)}
            >
              {s}
            </button>
          ))}
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

items.name: data-table
items.title: Data Table
items.description: A generic `DataTable<T>` built on a CSS grid, not a `<table>`, so rows can move: click a column to cycle sort ascending, descending, off and the rows FLIP to their new positions with a layout animation rather than snapping. Any column can carry a `bar` accessor that paints a proportional fill behind its value, so the table reads as a chart too. Headers resize by dragging their edge, with a live guide line and a shared `gridTemplateColumns` string driving header and every row. Row selection is controlled (`selectedIds` / `onSelectedIdsChange`) and raises a floating action bar; a `loading` prop swaps in a shimmer-swept skeleton, an empty dataset shows an empty state, and a density prop animates row height. Real ARIA table roles with `aria-sort`, status shown by dot plus label not color alone, and a reduced-motion path that drops the row slide and bar grow.

items.name: table-toolbar
items.title: Table Toolbar
items.description: The control strip that sits above a table, holding only state you pass in: a search value, a selected-values map per faceted filter, and a hidden-columns list. The search field is the library's own Search Input, installed as a dependency. Each faceted filter opens a multi-select menu with per-option counts, every active choice becomes a removable pill on a second row, and one Reset clears search and every facet together. A View menu toggles column visibility, and a right-aligned `actions` slot takes export or add-row buttons. Menus close on outside click or Escape, animate in with a reduced-motion path, and every control has a visible focus ring.

items.name: table-pagination
items.title: Table Pagination
items.description: The footer bar for a paged table: a live range label (11 to 20 of 247) that swaps to a selection count when rows are checked, and an optional rows-per-page select that resets to page one. The page-number nav is the library's own Pagination component, installed as a dependency, so the ellipsis collapsing and the sliding active-page highlight are not reimplemented here. `Pagination` was upgraded to a controlled `page` / `pageCount` / `onPageChange` API and now exports a `paginationRange(page, pageCount, siblings)` helper.

items.name: expandable-table
items.title: Expandable Rows Table
items.description: A real `<table>` where each row has a caret that reveals a detail panel spanning the full width, animated open and closed by height with a reduced-motion path that cuts straight to the final state. Expansion is tracked as a set of row ids so several rows can stay open at once, the toggle carries `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the panel, and the detail renderer is a prop so the panel can hold anything: a sub-table, a form, a timeline.

items.name: tree-table
items.title: Tree Table
items.description: A `treegrid` for hierarchical rows: branches expand and collapse, depth is shown by indentation with a connector line, and parent rows roll up a numeric column from their descendants so a collapsed folder still shows its total size. It flattens a nested tree into visible rows on each render, keyboard support follows the tree pattern (right and left to open and close, arrows to move), and expanded state is a controlled set of ids.

items.name: sticky-column-table
items.title: Pinned Column Table
items.description: A wide table that scrolls horizontally while the first column (and an optional trailing actions column) stays frozen with `position: sticky`. Pass `maxHeight` and it becomes a spreadsheet frozen-pane grid: the header row and the pinned column both hold while the body scrolls on both axes, so a trackpad diagonal swipe moves through the grid diagonally in one gesture. Each of the four edges carries a shadow that fades in only while there is content scrolled behind it, driven by a real scroll listener measuring all four offsets, so a seam reads as depth rather than a static border. Pinned cells and the header corner sit above the rest on the z-axis so nothing bleeds through.

items.name: editable-table
items.title: Editable Table
items.description: Click a cell to edit it in place: text cells become inputs, enum cells become selects, Enter commits and moves down, Tab commits and moves right, Escape reverts. Edits are staged per row, so a changed row shows a dot and a Save or Revert pair rather than writing through on every keystroke, and committing calls back with the whole patched row. Cell type and validation come from the column config, and an invalid value blocks the commit with an inline message.

items.name: comparison-table
items.title: Comparison Table
items.description: A feature matrix for pricing or product tiers: the feature-name column is pinned left, one column is marked recommended (its badge is the library's own Badge) and stays tinted across every row, and cells accept a boolean (check or dash), a string, or partial support. Rows group under section headers, the header row with the tier names and prices sticks to the top on scroll, and support is shown by icon plus text so it does not rely on color. Degrades to a horizontally scrollable card on narrow screens.

items.name: metrics-table
items.title: Metrics Table
items.description: A dashboard leaderboard assembled from the library's own Data Table, not a fresh table: five `DataColumn` definitions give a fixed rank, a label, the primary metric with Data Table's `bar` accessor painting the in-cell fill, a trend delta (arrow plus signed percentage, colour and glyph together), and a self-drawing inline sparkline. Sorting, `aria-sort`, column resize and the FLIP row reorder are all inherited. Installing it pulls in `data-table`; the `Sparkline` and `TrendDelta` helpers are exported for reuse in your own columns.

items.name: link-preview-card
items.title: Link Preview Card
items.description: A rich unfurl card for hyperlinking to anything with a UI or an image, like pasting a link into Slack or Notion: a mocked screenshot thumbnail by default, a real `image` (plus an optional `credit`) for an actual photo with a click-through attribution chip, or a `liveUrl` to embed the real destination page itself, scaled down, as a genuinely live thumbnail rather than a static shot. The thumbnail zooms slightly on hover, an external-link icon fades in over the domain, and the card resolves through a real shimmering skeleton first, timed to the iframe's own `onLoad` event when `liveUrl` is used, so the loading state reflects an actual fetch.

items.name: intelligent-empty-state
items.title: Intelligent Empty State
items.description: A blank workspace that actually evolves instead of staying blank forever, driven by a real visit count and real click counts kept in this browser, not a scripted slideshow: visit one highlights a single guided action with a pulsing halo, visits two through four recap exactly what you did last time, and visit five on promotes whichever action you've actually clicked most into a one-tap sparkle shortcut. A "simulate next visit" control lets you fast-forward through all three tiers in one sitting.

items.name: pill-tabs
items.title: Pill Tabs
items.description: A segmented tab control with a sliding active state, uncontrolled by default but usable as a controlled toggle (`active` plus `onChange`) for driving other UI from the selected tab, with `showPanels` to opt out of the auto-rendered tab-content stubs when you're supplying your own panel.

items.name: breadcrumbs
items.title: Breadcrumbs
items.description: A simple breadcrumb trail with an aria-current page marker.

items.name: command-palette
items.title: Command Palette
items.description: A ⌘K search overlay with grouped fuzzy results, arrow-key navigation, and a sliding highlight; this very page uses it to jump between sections.

items.name: pagination
items.title: Pagination
items.description: A controlled numbered page control (`page` / `pageCount` / `onPageChange`): prev and next, numeric buttons that collapse to ellipses around the current page past seven pages, and a sliding active-page highlight on a shared layoutId (the same technique as Pill Tabs). Exports the `paginationRange(page, pageCount, siblings)` helper that builds the number-and-gap list. Table Pagination wraps this with a range label and page-size select.

items.name: stepper
items.title: Stepper
items.description: A multi-step progress indicator whose connecting lines fill and whose completed steps draw in a checkmark.

items.name: icon-stepper
items.title: Icon Stepper
items.description: A stepper with a swappable per-step icon instead of a number: the demo's own icon set swap button proves it, live.

items.name: comet-stepper
items.title: Comet Stepper
items.description: Advancing sends a glowing comet racing along the connector, the arriving step bursts with a ring pulse, and every badge face-swaps with a 3D flip; multi-step jumps cascade left to right.

items.name: dropdown-menu
items.title: Dropdown Menu
items.description: A click-triggered menu with a spring-in panel, sliding hover highlight, and full keyboard navigation.

items.name: dock-nav
items.title: Dock Nav
items.description: A floating, physics-magnified dock in the shape of macOS's own: icons grow the closer your cursor gets to them, tracked per-icon off a single shared pointer position, and pop upward as they magnify. Scroll the panel and it tucks itself out of view, then springs back the moment you scroll up, the same behavior you'd get pinning it `fixed` to the bottom of a real page.

items.name: rail-nav
items.title: Rail Nav
items.description: A top nav bar that collapses to its mobile menu off its own measured width via ResizeObserver, not a CSS breakpoint: nest it in a sidebar and it still gets it right. A shared sliding pill tracks whichever link is hovered, hovering "Product" or "Solutions" drops a live mega-panel of preview tiles beneath the bar, and a soft glow trails the pointer along the top edge. Switch the frame to "Mobile" to see the same component fall back to a slide-down menu.

items.name: sidebar-nav
items.title: Sidebar Nav
items.description: The left app-shell sidebar most SaaS dashboards actually ship (Linear, Notion, Vercel): drag its right edge to resize it, or drag past the collapse point and it snaps into a 64px icon-only rail, the same click-the-hamburger toggle works too, with labels shrinking away in place and a hover tooltip standing in for them. A real workspace switcher and search sit up top, grouped links carry a sliding active highlight, a badge count becomes a small dot once collapsed, and the footer is a working presence switcher (Online/Away/Do not disturb/Offline) instead of a static profile card. Switch the frame to "Mobile" to see the same hamburger button open a slide-in drawer over a backdrop instead of collapsing in place.

items.name: strata-menu
items.title: Strata Menu
items.description: A right-side drawer menu for deep trees. Stepping into a submenu slides a fresh panel in from the right; every level you leave folds into a labeled vertical panel stacked at the drawer's left edge. The fold is not just a breadcrumb: hover or focus a folded panel and it opens an amber preview of that whole level, with your current branch still marked in green, so you can jump straight to a sibling without walking back up. Arrow keys move within a level, right steps in, left steps back, Escape unwinds one step at a time; the drawer is a focus-trapped role=dialog that traps Tab and restores focus to the trigger. Theme-aware on the library's slate, emerald, and amber palette, the whole tree is one recursive structure so depth is just data, and every transition collapses to a crossfade under prefers-reduced-motion. Its lineage is Julian Fella's stacked drawer, extended with the peek-and-jump layer and full keyboard traversal.

items.name: popover
items.title: Popover
items.description: The anchored-panel primitive that Tooltip and Dropdown Menu each solve privately, extracted once. A placement engine tries the preferred side, flips to the opposite when the panel would overflow that edge, then shifts along the cross axis to stay inside the boundary and repoints the arrow at the trigger center; it recomputes on scroll and resize. The demo anchor is draggable so you can watch it correct itself. The shipped component is a portal trigger plus `content`, controlled or uncontrolled, with click-outside and Escape to close and a reduced-motion path.

items.name: reveal-on-scroll
items.title: Reveal on Scroll
items.description: Fades and lifts content in the first time it enters the viewport.

items.name: logo-wall
items.title: Logo Wall
items.description: A trusted-by grid where the empty cells and the photo cells answer the same hover in two different currencies: a plain cell inverts its own background and text in a circular wipe that grows from wherever the cursor actually entered it, while a photo cell stays blurred and translucent everywhere except a small sharp spotlight that tracks the cursor in real time, genuinely masked pixel-for-pixel rather than a swapped image. Photo credits surface only on hover, bottom-right of their own cell.

items.name: marquee
items.title: Marquee
items.description: An infinitely looping horizontal scroller built on a Framer Motion animate loop.

items.name: parallax
items.title: Parallax
items.description: A useParallax hook plus a ParallaxLayer wrapper for scroll-linked depth: layers drift at different speeds as the page scrolls, bound to enter, exit, or the full time a section is in view.

items.name: card-stack-scroll
items.title: Card Stack Scroll
items.description: A vertical stack of cards pinned via position: sticky, one shared scroll progress driving every card's scale so each shrinks and peeks out from behind the next as you scroll past it. Exposes a ref handle with scrollToId/scrollToIndex, animating exactly that container's own scroll position with a custom easing rather than the native scrollIntoView, so an outside nav can jump to a card without dragging the surrounding page along with it.

items.name: spotlight-card
items.title: Spotlight Card
items.description: A card with a radial glow that follows the cursor, bound via a motion value.

items.name: magnetic-button
items.title: Magnetic Button
items.description: A button that pulls toward the cursor within a radius on two independently-sprung layers, then snaps back on leave.

items.name: tooltip
items.title: Tooltip
items.description: A hover/focus tooltip that springs in and flips from top to bottom automatically near the edge of its container.

items.name: infinite-moving-cards
items.title: Infinite Moving Cards
items.description: Like Marquee, but scrolling full testimonial cards in two independently-directed, pause-on-hover rows.

items.name: text-generate-effect
items.title: Text Generate Effect
items.description: Words sharpen into focus one at a time as the paragraph enters the viewport, blur-to-sharp rather than a plain fade.

items.name: resource-scheduler
items.title: Resource Scheduler
items.description: A resource scheduling calendar with Today, Day, Week, and Month views. In the time views, resources (Day) or the seven days of the week (Week) run across as sticky columns with time down the vertical axis; one shared column engine positions every block (including overlap lanes) for both, so there is no per-view code. Drag a block across columns and time slots in one gesture, resize it from either edge (15-minute snap, live snap guide, siblings reflow with a spring, dropped blocks settle home), or tap it to edit. Tapping a block or hitting New opens one editor: a popover anchored under the New button with a caret pointing at it, so it never reads as a menu off the view tabs; the grid never reflows, and Escape, the scrim, or any navigation closes it. Booking over another meeting on the same resource shows a non-blocking overlap notice, the time fields are bounded scroll pickers rather than a native select, and dragging a block to the top or bottom edge auto-scrolls the day. A custom month-grid date picker jumps the calendar or an event's day. Month is a full grid overview with quick create and edit. Column headers are real Avatars, the range count is a real Badge, and each resource carries one of the library's own accent tones (emerald, amber, rose, slate) so an event's colour is its resource's colour and a cross-column drag recolours it. A live now-line, keyboard nudging, and reduced-motion support are built in.

items.name: orbit-loader
items.title: Orbit Loader
items.description: Two dots orbit a swappable center icon; pass your own product's mark via the icon prop.

items.name: pulse-loader
items.title: Pulse Loader
items.description: A sonar-pulse loading indicator; pass your own product's mark via the icon prop.

items.name: thinking-loader
items.title: Thinking Loader
items.description: A spinning icon beside a word that cycles through a swappable list ("Thinking", "Finagling"...) with a trailing pulsing ellipsis, in the spirit of Claude Code's own status line; both the icon and the word list are optional props.

items.name: empty-state
items.title: Empty State
items.description: An empty-state panel with a floating inbox icon, breathing waiting rings, and an optional action.

items.name: success-state
items.title: Success State
items.description: A confirmation panel with a spring-in checkmark, a confirm ring burst, and a particle scatter.

items.name: error-state
items.title: Error State
items.description: An error panel with a shake animation and an urgency-pulsed halo.

items.name: attention-gradient
items.title: Attention Gradient
items.description: A notification list where urgency is a computed number, not a fixed color-coded badge: each channel tracks how many times in a row it's been ignored, and that count directly drives a continuously blended slate-to-amber-to-rose glow plus an ambient pulse that speeds up as it climbs, both real interpolations of the same value rather than swapped CSS classes. Open a channel and it snaps straight back to calm; keep dismissing it with "Not now" and it visibly escalates, with a plain-language readout ("Ignored 2 times in a row") explaining exactly why.

items.name: recovery-diff
items.title: Recovery Diff
items.description: A connection form where a failed check explains itself inline instead of just saying something went wrong: a real character-level diff, computed against whatever you actually typed, highlights exactly what differs field by field, and a one-click fix button applies that specific field's correct value rather than offering a generic retry. Fix one field and its diff panel collapses immediately; get every field right and an inline success line confirms it, no modal anywhere in the flow.

items.name: scope-preview
items.title: Scope Preview
items.description: A calendar connection request where the permission list isn't the whole story: toggle any scope and a live preview panel recomputes what the connection could actually do, down to a genuine two-scope combination (read plus create) that unlocks a real "Add to calendar" action neither scope enables alone. Hover a scope and the exact preview line it powers highlights in place, so the abstract checkbox and the concrete consequence are never more than a glance apart.

items.name: consent-ledger
items.title: Consent Ledger
items.description: A permissions list where every grant stays individually revocable in the same view, not filed away in a settings sub-menu: the same switch that revokes a grant restores it, instantly, no confirmation dialog either direction. A dependency panel underneath shows exactly which mocked features that grant was powering, and the moment it's revoked, an animated strike draws itself across every feature that actually needed it, live.

items.name: cost-preview
items.title: Cost Preview
items.description: A compute-scaling slider where the commit button states the real consequence itself, a genuine prorated charge or credit computed live from the days left in the billing cycle, instead of burying it in fine print elsewhere on the page. Drag past the current count and the instance list below names exactly which running instance would stop, last one added first, or which new one would start, before you've committed to anything, so scaling down and applying visibly removes those rows rather than just decrementing a number.

items.name: silent-failure-surface
items.title: Silent Failure Surface
items.description: A background-jobs panel built around one rule: nothing here ever turns red, however many times it fails. Repeated failures of the same job collapse into a single batched line with a real count, not one alarming toast per failure, and a working retry actually spins, waits, and resolves the streak back to a clean run rather than snapping straight to success. A per-job sparkline of the last six runs shows whether a job self-recovered on its own or is still waiting on a retry, at a glance.

items.name: presence-indicator
items.title: Presence Indicator
items.description: A stacked avatar cluster plus a live pulsing dot and a "N viewing" label, the real-time-collaboration cue Notion, Figma, and Google Docs each show somewhere in their own chrome, distinct from Avatar Group's hover-to-reveal trust row.

items.name: toast
items.title: Toast
items.description: A corner notification with a draining progress bar and drag-to-dismiss; swipe it away or let it time out.

items.name: dialog
items.title: Dialog
items.description: The modal primitive the rest of a library assumes exists: a focus-trapped `role="dialog"` with a real scrim, Escape and scrim-click and drag-the-panel-down to dismiss, body scroll lock, and focus returned to whatever opened it. The scrim is a clip-path iris that grows from the center of the trigger button (via an `originRef`) and collapses back into it on close. A `focusTracer` prop draws an outline that chases the keyboard focus around the panel and slides its full width, with a readout, the instant Tab wraps, so the trap is visible rather than just asserted. Dialogs mounted while another is open stack through a shared store: the one underneath scales back and dims, Escape only closes the top. Every animation degrades to a plain fade under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

items.name: alert
items.title: Alert
items.description: The inline callout, in four variants (info, success, warning, danger), each keyed by an icon and a left accent bar so it never relies on color alone; warning and danger take `role="alert"`. Optional `onDismiss` collapses the alert and lets a wrapping layout list slide up to close the gap, `details` adds a Show details height-animated disclosure, `action` a single button. Reduced motion drops the collapse for a fade.

items.name: progress
items.title: Progress
items.description: One `Progress` component covering the cases every app needs: `linear` or `circular`, determinate or `indeterminate`, in emerald, amber, or rose. The determinate linear fill carries a moving sheen until it hits 100 then pulses a ring out; the circular ring tweens its `strokeDashoffset` and shows the percentage in the center. Indeterminate is a sliding bar or a spinning arc. Correct `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow` / `aria-valuemin` / `aria-valuemax` when determinate and `aria-valuetext` when not, plus a reduced-motion path that drops every looping animation.

items.name: skeleton-loader
items.title: Skeleton Loader
items.description: A shimmer-swept placeholder card for loading states, with a static reduced-motion fallback.

items.name: undoable-action
items.title: Undoable Action
items.description: A delete that mutates in place through three real, timed levels of permanence: an instant Undo (fast draining bar), a quieter Recently Deleted holding pen with its own restore window (dashed border, slower drain), then a locked, grayscale, button-less permanently deleted state. Both countdowns are driven by real elapsed time, not a guessed CSS duration.

items.name: waiting-state
items.title: Waiting State
items.description: A deploy progress narrator with zero percentage bars: a connector line fills only as each real step actually completes, a live elapsed clock ticks on the active step, and watch "Building assets" run genuinely long, past its own typical estimate, triggering a calm "taking a little longer than usual" note instead of a bar that quietly stalls and lies. Every finished step keeps its real measured duration on screen.

items.name: permission-negotiator
items.title: Permission Negotiator
items.description: A single-capability permission ask, requested in context instead of dumped upfront, switchable between two real examples: microphone (typed-note fallback) and camera (a genuine live video preview, mirrored, bound to the real stream, with a palette-color-avatar fallback). Click "Try it" and it asks your real browser with a genuine getUserMedia call, not a fake dialog. Decline either one and the feature keeps working in its fallback rather than breaking, with a quiet, always-available "Enable" link, no re-ask nagging, no dead end either way.

items.name: honest-retry
items.title: Honest Retry
items.description: A rate-limited request that explains itself instead of spinning forever: a plain-language reason for the wait, a live countdown ticking on real elapsed time (not a decorative animation), and a Retry now override that's honest about what it does, it skips straight to the next real attempt rather than faking success. Backs off twice on its own before it gets through, each failure re-stating why in the same spot.

items.name: ambiguous-input-resolver
items.title: Ambiguous Input Resolver
items.description: Stands in for whatever guesses at intent, autocomplete, voice, an AI parser, and shows its interpretation as editable pills inline in the reassembled sentence before anything commits, instead of silently acting on its best guess. A genuinely ambiguous slot (two contacts named Sarah, "next Tuesday" reading either week) opens a small dropdown with its alternates ranked and the reason it's unsure; a confident slot still opens the same dropdown to show there was only one real match. Confirming locks in whatever's currently selected, corrected in place or not.

items.name: batch-action-preview
items.title: Batch Action Preview
items.description: A bulk tag rename that shows the real per-item outcome instead of a bare "4 items selected" count: every affected task lists its own before/after tag diff, and one of them behaves differently from the rest, it already has the target tag, so the rename merges instead of duplicating, called out inline rather than hidden behind a uniform-looking batch. Uncheck any task to exclude it before committing, and the applied summary states what actually happened (renamed vs. merged) rather than a flat total.

items.name: draft-recovery
items.title: Draft Recovery
items.description: A note field backed by real browser storage, not component state: pause while typing and it autosaves, and a genuine remount (via the demo's own "simulate crash" control, or an actual page reload, since the storage is real) brings the text back on its own with a brief, non-blocking banner, never a "we found a draft, restore?" dialog asking permission to give you back your own work.

items.name: comparison-diff
items.title: Comparison Diff
items.description: AI-suggested prose edits rendered as a real word-level inline diff, computed against the actual before/after text rather than a canned highlight, one hunk per sentence, each accepted, rejected, or undone independently. An "Accept rest" shortcut clears whatever's still pending without forcing a read of every hunk, and undo works after the fact on either decision, so nothing a reviewer picks is final until they're done.

items.name: ambient-save-indicator
items.title: Ambient Save Indicator
items.description: A save status that stays a small, low-contrast dot and label next to the field it's saving, never a corner toast, and only grows loud when there's something to actually act on: flip on "Simulate save failures" and the same spot expands, real layout animation, into a full rose bar naming how many changes aren't backed up yet, with a working retry. Fix it and it shrinks straight back to quiet.

items.name: multi-device-handoff
items.title: Multi-Device Handoff
items.description: A checkout that states exactly what it found before touching anything: source device, how long ago, which step, and the live cart total, with Continue and Start fresh as two genuinely different, equally valid paths rather than one silent default. Continuing keeps a persistent "Resumed from iPhone" tag on screen (with its own one-click way back to fresh) instead of quietly populating the form and hoping nobody asks where the data came from; starting fresh says plainly that the other session's progress is untouched, not deleted.

items.name: session-timeout-warning
items.title: Session Timeout Warning
items.description: A real countdown to session expiry (`performance.now()`-driven, not a guessed CSS duration) that surfaces a "Stay signed in" warning with genuine lead time rather than an ambush, and a draft textarea that proves the point of the whole pattern: it's still fully intact, untouched by any state transition, on the other side of an actual expiry, merely disabled until "Sign back in" resolves. No login-page redirect anywhere in the flow, in-flight work never has a chance to be at risk.

items.name: disagreement-resolver
items.title: Disagreement Resolver
items.description: Two conflicting signals (a fraud rule vs. a risk model on one order, two separate AI review passes on one contract clause, switchable via chips) shown side by side with each one's own verdict and reasoning, instead of one silently overriding the other before a person ever sees the conflict. Resolving records which one a reviewer trusted, sends both to manual review, or gets undone after the fact, but the losing signal stays fully visible and readable, just dimmed, never erased from the record.

items.name: chat-input-bar
items.title: Chat Input Bar
items.description: An AI-chat composer with an always-on ambient glow: real permission-gated mic recording with playback, attach and new-conversation icons, a model-picker dropdown, and a send button that morphs into a stoppable 'thinking' state.

items.name: chain-of-thought
items.title: Chain of Thought
items.description: A live agent reasoning trace: a hand-drawn connector line fills as each step resolves, a real elapsed-time counter ticks while it works, and it auto-collapses into a 'Thought for 2.8s' summary pill once done; replay it any time.

items.name: reasoning
items.title: Reasoning
items.description: Raw model reasoning streaming word-by-word into an auto-scrolling, fade-masked panel with a blinking cursor; collapses into a duration pill when finished, just like extended thinking in Claude or ChatGPT.

items.name: confirmation
items.title: Confirmation
items.description: An inline tool-call approval card with a risk-tiered badge; destructive actions require a genuine press-and-hold to approve (the fill animates as you hold and snaps back if you let go early), so nothing catastrophic fires from a stray click.

items.name: confidence-slider
items.title: Confidence Slider
items.description: A confidence meter that doesn't just relabel itself, it hands you a different amount of control: drag past 75% and one tap accepts the answer, drop below 40% and every generated claim needs its own confirm-or-flag before Accept will even enable, with the whole panel morphing shape live as you cross each threshold. An ambient glow breathes behind the thumb, the tier badge and claim icons pop in rather than snapping, and the Accept button gives a genuine spring-and-ring unlock pulse the instant it actually becomes pressable.

items.name: decision-timeline
items.title: Decision Timeline
items.description: A plan recommendation that shows its actual math: four weighted factors, each with its own mute switch and a magnitude bar, sum to a live, tween-animated point total against a visible threshold. Mute the biggest factor and watch the recommendation genuinely flip, Pro to Starter, with a shared-layout sliding pill, not just a relabeled badge; this is real, inspectable arithmetic driving the outcome, not a canned explanation.

items.name: interruptible-automation
items.title: Interruptible Automation
items.description: A bulk file-organizer that runs itself, but genuinely pauses at flagged files instead of only offering a kill switch: a live dot rail tracks all six files by status, and each checkpoint slides in with the exact next move, a plain-language reason it's unsure, and an editable destination picker with a sliding pill, so you can redirect the file before it commits, skip it, or stop the whole run at any moment and leave the rest untouched.

items.name: sources
items.title: Sources
items.description: Perplexity-style citations: numbered inline markers and their source cards highlight each other bidirectionally on hover or focus, collapsed by default behind a fanned favicon stack.

items.name: suggestion
items.title: Suggestion
items.description: A row of quick-reply chips with a fade-masked scroll edge; picking one flies it into a composer-preview pill instead of just vanishing, and a shuffle button swaps in a fresh batch with a staggered spring.

items.name: tool
items.title: Tool
items.description: A tool-call card that shows the whole round trip: the status pill morphs queued → running → streaming → success (or failed), a green sheen sweeps the input row as the args dispatch, the result then types itself in key by key with a caret, and the hairline under the header is a latency rail that sweeps while the call is in flight, then locks to the measured duration against a p50 tick (with a faster/slower delta). Header collapses the body, replay re-runs the same outcome, reduced motion drops the sweep and typewriter for a plain reveal. Try both outcomes with the demo's own toggle.

items.name: artifact
items.title: Artifact
items.description: A generated-file panel that shimmers in like it's being written, keeps a real version history you can scrub between, and expands into a true fullscreen modal via a shared-layout morph; copy and download both actually work.

items.name: code-block
items.title: Code Block
items.description: A multi-file, tabbed code snippet with a copy button; the live preview here is highlighted by this site's own CodeBlock component, the same one rendering every code panel on this page. The copyable snippet ships a small self-contained tokenizer instead, since it can't depend on this site's build-time highlighter.

items.name: commit
items.title: Commit
items.description: An agent-authored commit message streams in word by word, then the hash (genuinely derived from the message text via a small hash function, not hardcoded), and file stats pop in, with an expandable per-file diff summary.

items.name: commit-graph
items.title: Commit Graph
items.description: A GitHub-style contribution heatmap with five swappable color themes (swatch picker included) and a streak badge that only shows once there's an actual streak. Clicking Commit round-trips through a simulated ~500ms backend call before today's cell levels up, since this site ships as a static export with no server to hold real state; the count it returns is persisted to localStorage the same way a server response would get cached, so it survives a reload without one. A production version would swap that mock for a real POST to /api/commits and read the count back from there instead.

items.name: file-tree
items.title: File Tree
items.description: A changed-files tree that builds itself in with a staggered cascade, like the agent is scaffolding it live; new/modified/deleted status is signaled by icon, label, and strikethrough, never color alone.

items.name: file-highlighter
items.title: File Highlighter
items.description: Drops inline file-path highlighting into a chat message: a real regex scan finds file-shaped tokens in plain prose (not a hardcoded list) and turns each into a syntax-badged chip that pops in as it's found. Chips the demo has a source file for expand into a small tokenized code snippet, accordion-style, one at a time; chips it doesn't recognize still highlight, they just don't expand.

items.name: sandbox
items.title: Sandbox
items.description: A container boot sequence that settles into a live 'Ready' state with a copyable preview URL and breathing CPU/memory gauges; restart it to watch the boot steps resolve again.

items.name: test-results
items.title: Test Results
items.description: A test suite runs sequentially with a live segmented pass/fail progress bar and a real elapsed-time counter; the one failing test expands in place to show its assertion message.

items.name: terminal
items.title: Terminal
items.description: Commands the agent runs get typed in character by character and their output streams line by line, auto-scrolling as it goes; settles into a blinking idle cursor once the sequence finishes.

items.name: audio-player
items.title: Audio Player
items.description: A voice-reply player backed by a real audio file: a genuinely click-and-drag-to-seek waveform (full keyboard support too, arrow keys, Home/End, Space), a mute toggle with a slim volume slider, a playback-speed cycle button, and controls to swap in your own audio file or delete it entirely.

items.name: audio-scrubber
items.title: Audio Scrubber
items.description: The same real-audio voice-reply player (swap-in/delete audio included), but the seek control is a Spotify-style progress rail: a slim track that thickens on hover and reveals a circular thumb, instead of a bar-height waveform.

items.name: persona
items.title: Persona
items.description: An AI agent identity card with an abstract gradient 'orb' avatar instead of a human avatar; switching between personas briefly flashes a 'Thinking' status before crossfading to the new persona's traits.

items.name: transcription
items.title: Transcription
items.description: Live speech-to-text with a real interim/final distinction: press record and it transcribes what you actually say via the browser's Speech Recognition API, with words streaming in muted and italic while still being recognized, then settling into solid text once that phrase finalizes. Includes a language selector.

items.name: voice-selector
items.title: Voice Selector
items.description: A voice picker where auditioning a voice and selecting it are two separate actions, like real TTS pickers: each option gets its own preview button with a pulsing ring while it 'plays', independent of which voice is actually selected, and every avatar bobs on its own idle cycle and does a small bounce on preview, so the grid reads as alive rather than static. Defaults to four realistic voices (Ember, Sable, Flux, Vale) with abstract gradient-orb avatars, the same 'identity without a literal mascot' idea as this library's own Persona card; a 'Fun avatars' toggle swaps the whole set for four illustrated GIF animals with gender-neutral given names (River, Sage, Robin, Kit), demonstrating the avatar slot is a genuinely pluggable seam rather than one hardcoded look.

items.name: attachments
items.title: Attachments
items.description: A file tray with a real native file picker: files you actually add get their real name and size and start 'uploading' with a per-item circular progress ring; one demo file fails on purpose so you can see the retry flow.

items.name: settings-panel
items.title: Settings Panel
items.description: The two-pane settings dialog every AI chat app converges on, in the mold of Claude's and ChatGPT's own: a live sidebar search, a grouped sliding-highlight tab list, and an Accent color picker that actually retints every focus ring, button, and toggle in the dialog the instant you pick a new one, not just its own swatch. Every field genuinely autosaves (switch tabs or close and reopen the dialog and nothing resets) with a real 'Saving… / Saved' indicator, not a decorative one. A dismissible MFA banner morphs into a real confirmation on click, and the Profile pane's avatar recolors on click too.

items.name: app-widget
items.title: App Widget
items.description: The rich, app-branded result card a connected tool hands back inline in chat: the same pattern ChatGPT's and Claude's app/MCP connectors use to render real UI instead of plain text. Every instance opens gated behind a real "Sign in to {app}" step: with an `app.loginUrl` set, clicking it genuinely opens that product's real login page in a new tab (Spotify's and Figma's own, here) before spring-morphing into a "Connecting…" spinner and the live result, and that connection genuinely persists across visits (`localStorage`, a rolling 30-day expiry), so it only re-gates after a month of disuse rather than every reload. In `mode="live"` the result is the product's own official iframe (demoed here with Spotify's and Figma's real, live embeds, not a recreation), resolving from a genuine shimmering skeleton via the iframe's own `onLoad`. For apps with no embeddable surface, the default demo mode renders a hand-built card instead, generalized past music with a `resultKind` prop, "audio" (Preview/Pause, a live equalizer) or "document" (Open/Opened, a checkmark badge), plus real thumbs and a header action (a Devices menu or a Copy-link button that morphs to a checkmark), picked per instance.

items.name: ai-landing-template
items.title: AI Product Landing
items.description: A full agent-product landing page for 'Fielder': an interactive prompt hero (three scenario chips plus a Run it button that replays a real Confirmation approval card, and a hover-tooltip Avatar Group standing in for the trust row), a marquee logo strip, a tab-switched 'watch it handle a ticket' console where each of the four capability claims drives a different live component instead of static copy (Sources for the docs it cites, Tool for the refund it issues, a condensed Chain of Thought for its reasoning, a destructive-risk Confirmation for the escalation it holds for review), a second full Chain of Thought reasoning trail on a different ticket, an auto-scrolling testimonial row, count-up pricing in a Pricing Card, and an FAQ Accordion, wired from real library components (Marquee, Infinite Moving Cards, Sources, Tool, Confirmation, Chain of Thought, Pricing Card, Accordion, Avatar Group, Magnetic Button) rather than reimplemented inline.

items.name: saas-landing-template
items.title: SaaS Product Landing
items.description: A full marketing page for 'Ridgeline': an Apple-style oversized two-clause hero with a pinned-scale screenshot and drifting stat badges, a live counted-up stat bar, alternating feature rows tagged with a real Badge pill and each paired with its own real mini screenshot card (a capacity breakdown, a dependency chip, a mini kanban board) instead of a placeholder box, a chip nav that jumps between them, count-up pricing in a Pricing Card, and an FAQ Accordion, built on Pricing Card, Accordion, Badge, Magnetic Button, and the Testimonial Carousel.

items.name: premium-saas-homepage-template
items.title: Premium SaaS Homepage
items.description: A near-black, gold-accented enterprise marketing homepage for 'Meridian', a cash-intelligence platform for finance teams: a blurred-word-reveal hero headline next to a live instrument-panel mockup (a real Stat Card and Mini Chart), a trust-bar Marquee, a genuinely-ordered three-step 'how it works' row, a 3D cursor-tilt Spotlight Card feature bento, a card-less Pull Quote proof section backed by an Avatar Group, and a sales-led enterprise CTA with no self-serve pricing tier, deliberately structured differently from the other two templates (no FAQ, no tiered pricing grid, no isolated stat bar) so it doesn't share their skeleton. Built on Stat Card, Mini Chart, Marquee, Avatar Group, Spotlight Card, Pull Quote, Text Generate Effect, Hover Border Gradient, and Magnetic Button rather than reimplementing each of them inline.
